title: Crocchette di Patate
subtitle: Italian potato croquettes with mozzarella filling
excerpt: Crocchette di patate are Italian potato croquettes made from mashed potato seasoned with Parmesan and egg yolk, shaped into cylinders or ovals, filled with a small piece of mozzarella, and deep-fried until golden and crisp. The potato casing is light and savoury; the mozzarella melts inside. They are a staple of Italian fried street food and appear on every fritto misto.
sourceNotes: Crocchette di patate are a classic of Italian street food and antipasto, particularly in Naples and Rome. The filling of mozzarella or provola is standard in the southern Italian version. Artusi, La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene (1891), public domain, includes potato croquette preparations.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Shape and bread the croquettes up to 4 hours ahead. Keep in the fridge until ready to fry.

content.text: Crocchette di patate work best with a dry, floury potato variety such as Maris Piper or King Edward. Waxy potatoes produce a sticky mash that is difficult to shape and does not hold together when frying. The mash must be completely cool before shaping, and the shaped croquettes must be chilled before breading and frying to hold their shape.

items.prepNote: drained and cut into small cubes

content.text: Boil {{potatoes-floury}} of potato chunks in salted water until tender. Drain and return to the pan over a low heat for 2 minutes to drive off excess moisture. Mash until smooth -- no lumps. Allow to cool to room temperature.
Beat in {{egg-yolks}} of egg yolks, {{parmesan}} of grated Parmesan, {{nutmeg}} of nutmeg, and {{salt-table}} of salt. The mixture should be firm enough to shape. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.

Take 2 tablespoons of potato mixture and flatten it in your palm. Place a cube of {{mozzarella}} mozzarella in the centre and fold the potato around it, shaping into a cylinder about 6 cm long. Repeat with the remaining mixture.
Set up three bowls: {{plain-flour}} flour, {{eggs}} beaten eggs, and {{breadcrumbs-dried}} breadcrumbs. Roll each croquette in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs. Return to the fridge for 15 minutes.
Heat {{vegetable-oil}} of vegetable oil to 180C. Fry the croquettes in batches of 4 for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until deep golden. Drain and serve hot.

items.symptom: The croquettes burst open when frying
items.cause: The potato mixture was too wet, the croquettes were not chilled, or the oil was not hot enough and they sat in the oil too long.
items.fix: Dry the mash thoroughly before mixing, chill the shaped croquettes well, and fry at 180C with a good thermometer.

content.text: Crocchette di patate are eaten throughout Italy but are most closely associated with Neapolitan street food and the Roman Jewish kitchen. In Naples they are sold from friggitorie (frying shops) alongside pasta fritta, zeppole, and pizza fritta. The mozzarella filling is the southern Italian version. In other regions the croquette is plain or contains a small amount of ham. They appear alongside olive ascolane and supplì on every Italian fried appetiser platter.
